problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a globally convex, differentiable function f:E→ℝ with L-Lipschitz gradient, L>0. A minimizer exists within distance R≥0 of x0. Strong convexity is not assumed.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query x returns ∇f(x) exactly, for every history and oracle seed. No function values are supplied. Each gradient query counts as one oracle call.

distinctive_assumptions.label: quadratic_growth
distinctive_assumptions.details: Global quadratic growth with μ>0: for every x there exists a minimizer z such that (μ/2)‖x−z‖²≤f(x)−f(z). The minimizer may depend on x.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is an arbitrary real Hilbert space, without a finite-dimensional restriction. Only E, L and x0 are public; μ, R and ε are hidden. Allowed algorithms use one predetermined sequence ηt>0 in xt+1=xt−ηt∇f(xt), independent of the hidden parameters, and output the current iterate.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: For ε>0, the final iterate after the supplied fixed gradient-call budget must satisfy f(output)−f(xstar)≤ε for a global minimizer xstar.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap inequality holds almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The objective and quadratic-growth condition are classical. The additional requirement of a predetermined positive-step gradient sequence, independent of μ, R and ε, with final-iterate accuracy at an externally specified fixed budget makes this formulation a meaningful restricted variant.

descriptionHtml:
Gradient Descent with Quadratic Growth

We consider minimizing a differentiable convex function f:E→R on a real Hilbert space E with norm ∥⋅∥. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz, with L>0. At each point, the objective gap is at least μ/2 times the squared distance to some global minimizer, where μ>0. A given starting point x0∈E lies within distance R≥0 of a global minimizer x⋆. The oracle returns ∇f(x) at x. For ε>0, gradient descent with positive predetermined step sizes must return a last iterate x¯ satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives only E, L, and x0; the parameters μ, R, and ε may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity). For every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y).

Assumption 2 (Smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E, and its gradient satisfies ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈E.

Assumption 3 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Assumption 4 (Quadratic growth). For every x∈E, there exists a global minimizer z∈E, possibly depending on x, such that μ2∥x−z∥2≤f(x)−f(z).

Our result is algorithm-specific: we analyze gradient descent. The step-size sequence (ηt)t≥0 is chosen from the algorithm inputs and satisfies ηt>0 for every t. Starting from the given x0, the iterates obey xt+1=xt−ηt∇f(xt),t=0,1,2,…. After K≥0 oracle calls, where K is an integer, the output is the last iterate x¯=xK. The required accuracy is f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s., where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness; the specified gradient descent method is deterministic.

comparisonHtml:
Convex f on a real Hilbert space has an exact L-Lipschitz gradient, L,μ,ε>0, and a minimizer x⋆ with ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, R≥0. For every x, some minimizer z satisfies f(x)−f(z)≥μ2∥x−z∥2. The setup restricts algorithms to GD with predetermined positive stepsizes and current-iterate output. Target: f(xK)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely. In (1), updates use only L; μ,R,ε enter the stopping budget.

(2) Restarted AGD (Fercoq and Qu 2017, Thm. 2, Sec. 3.4) O(1+κ[ℓ+log⁡(1+κ)])
Includes restart tests; smooth unconstrained specialization in Rd.		 (1): Predetermined GD with anytime last-iterate accuracy; (2) adaptively restarts AGD and returns a stopped output. No complexity improvement; updates already need no μ. (1): Exponent p instead of 1/2, with extra logarithms; requires global QG instead of initial-sublevel QG.
(3) Anytime GD (Zhang et al. 2025, Thm. 11, arXiv v2) O(κqℓ)
Special case: μ-strong convexity in Rd.		 (1): Scope: QG instead of strong convexity. Adaptivity: no μ. Rate on overlap: p≈0.786 instead of q≈0.893; total gain when κq−p≫1+log⁡κ+log⁡ℓ. (1): Extra 1+log⁡κ+log⁡ℓ factor. Crossover depends on unspecified constants; the unit-constant illustration exceeds κ≈1015.
(4) Silver GD (Altschuler and Parrilo 2023, Thm. 1.1) O(κpℓ)
Special case: μ-strong convexity; prescribed horizons. Distance contraction converted to objective gap.		 (1): Scope: QG instead of strong convexity. Adaptivity: neither κ nor horizon needed; anytime last-iterate accuracy instead of prescribed-horizon accuracy. (1): Extra 1+log⁡κ+log⁡ℓ factor on the strongly convex overlap.
(5) Restarted long-step GD (Grimmer et al. 2024, Remark 3) O((1+κ)pℓ)
Derived bound: convex PL restart in Rd; QG implies PL up to universal factors. Block-end objective accuracy.		 (1): No μ needed to choose block lengths; anytime last-iterate accuracy instead of block-end accuracy. Matches the condition-number exponent; no QG scope gain. (1): Extra 1+log⁡(1+κ)+log⁡ℓ factor.
(6) Constant-step GD, 1/L (Fercoq and Qu 2017, sec. 2.1) O((1+κ)ℓ)
QG/PL specialization of the classical proximal-gradient bound.		 (1): Rate: κ0.786 instead of κ, up to logarithms; total gain when κ1−p≫1+log⁡κ+log⁡ℓ. No adaptivity gain: (6) is already anytime and μ-free. (1): Larger leading constants and logarithmic overhead; savings require sufficiently large κ.

Abbr: Costs count exact gradient calls. κ=L/μ, ℓ=1+log⁡(1+LR2/ε), p=log⁡2/log⁡(1+2), q=(1+p)/2. GD: gradient descent; AGD: accelerated gradient descent; QG: quadratic growth; PL: Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality. Anytime: accuracy at every sufficiently large iteration; (1) exports the stated stopping budget.

import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import LongTails.Template

namespace LongTails.Setups.SmoothConvexQuadraticGrowth

open OracleTemplate

noncomputable def gradientMethod {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    (η : ℕ → ℝ) (x0 : E) : Algorithm E E E where
  State := ℕ × E
  initial _ := (0, x0)
  query s := (0, s.2)
  update s reply := (s.1 + 1, s.2 - η s.1 • reply)
  output s := s.2

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  L : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.completeE

structure Params extends Public where
  μ : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 < q.μ ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f oracle :=
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f ∧
    (∀ k seed x, HasGradientAt f (oracle.answer k (0, x) seed) x) ∧
    (∀ k seed x y, ‖oracle.answer k (0, x) seed - oracle.answer k (0, y) seed‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R) ∧
    (∀ x, ∃ z, IsMinOn f Set.univ z ∧ q.μ / 2 * ‖x - z‖ ^ 2 ≤ f x - f z)
  successful q f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), f (output ω) - f xstar ≤ q.ε
  allowedAlgorithm p algorithm :=
    ∃ η : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ t, 0 < η t) ∧ algorithm = gradientMethod η p.x0

end LongTails.Setups.SmoothConvexQuadraticGrowth
